QnA 1 · What does the final MGP stage change?

MGP optimizes the runtime model plan and prepares its routines for code generation. The compiler can now reason about storage, dependency chains and work shared across executions. The stage ends by emitting Mojo source for the later kernel compiler. It operates on IR1; G1 remains the caller's original graph. ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:382 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:484 ↗ FrameworkFrontend.cpp:377

Option or condition Native effect in this stage
kernelLibraryPaths Supplies primitive lowering and generated package imports
minimumCpuAlignment Passed into primitive lowering
enableOpTraceComments Controls comments attached by EmitMojoState

The options are copied in gcPipelineImpl and forwarded at the actual pass-construction sites. skipJit surrounds the later JIT passes, not the MGP transformations or EmitMojo itself. Option copies Emitter/profile options JIT branch

QnA 2 · Show canonicalization and chain simplification with actual values.

A static dimension query can become an integer constant. TensorSpecGetDimOp::fold reads the static dimension from the spec type and returns an IntegerAttr(index,dim). For a dynamic dimension created from an SSA operand, it can instead forward that operand. ↗ MGPOps.cpp:484

Static attention spec: <[32,32], f32>

BEFORE                             AFTER folding
  get_dim(%spec, axis=0)              32 : index
  get_dim(%spec, axis=1)              32 : index

Illustrative byte-count arithmetic
  32 × 32 × 4                        4096 bytes

After constants are materialized, eligible CSE can share identical
constant definitions. Q/K/V/O still identify different tensor storage.

TEST · inspected expectation: the chain tests eliminate duplicate dependencies, flatten nested merges and remove dependencies already implied by another chain. A chain is a completion dependency; simplifying its graph does not evaluate attention. ↗ mgp-simplify-chains.mlir:11 ↗ mgp-simplify-chains.mlir:108 ↗ mgp-simplify-chains.mlir:134

BEFORE                             AFTER simplifying dependencies
  c1 = merge(c0)                      use c0
  c2 = merge(c0,c0)                   use c0
  c3 = merge(merge(a,b),c)            merge(a,b,c)

If b is produced by work already dependent on a:
  merge(a,b)                          use b

The dependency is preserved; the redundant merge node is removed.

This does not authorize removing an actual kernel call whose returned chain is unused. Compiled calls can read and write pointed-to buffers; their side effects must remain. ↗ MOGGOps.td:444

QnA 3 · Can equal-sized buffers be reused? Give a numerical example.

Equal size is only one condition. SimpleBufferReusePass groups allocations by the same size SSA value, device and alignment. It then checks that every use of the later allocation executes after every use of the earlier candidate. A shared use by one operation explicitly rejects aliasing. ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:29 ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:77 ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:157

SimpleBufferReusePass::runOnOperation ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:95
├─ group buffer.alloc operations by (size SSA value, device, alignment) ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:112
├─ collect uses and obtain dependency ordering ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:120 ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:131
├─ reject buffers used by the same operation ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:157
└─ safe later use → replace uses with candidate buffer; erase allocation ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:169

TEST · inspected expectation: a serial three-kernel example reuses the first temporary for the third temporary. The middle temporary remains separate. A companion case retains all three allocations when sizes differ. ↗ mgp-simple-buffer-reuse.mlir:3 ↗ mgp-simple-buffer-reuse.mlir:29 ↗ mgp-simple-buffer-reuse.mlir:53

Comparison graph · three serial kernels, 4096-byte temporaries

BEFORE
  k0: input → A
  k1: A     → B
  k2: B     → C
  allocations: A + B + C = 3 × 4096 = 12288 bytes

AFTER eligible reuse
  k0: input → A
  k1: A     → B
  k2: B     → A       former A contents are no longer needed
  allocations: A + B = 2 × 4096 = 8192 bytes

Illustrative allocation capacity saving: 4096 bytes.
This is not a measurement of GPU peak memory or this attention graph.

For the single attention call, Q/K/V/O are used by the same computation. Their equal 4096-byte payloads do not permit the reuse transformation above. Q/K/V are also caller inputs, rather than three fresh temporary allocations created by this pass. ↗ SimpleBufferReusePass.cpp:157 ↗ LoweringState.cpp:808 ↗ fused_attention.py:78

QnA 4 · What can move from execute to init, and what becomes a context slot?

Execution-invariant motion can lift eligible work out of the repeated execute region. When later execution still needs a lifted buffer, the pass stores it through the init context and replaces execute-side uses with a cached-buffer lookup. It also supports cached indices, allocating a slot by increasing numSlots. ↗ ExecInvariantCodeMotionPass.cpp:80 ↗ ExecInvariantCodeMotionPass.cpp:822

Comparison · eligible invariant buffer, schematic

BEFORE
  init:     context(numSlots=0)
  execute:  build buffer W from invariant inputs → use W

AFTER eligible lift + cache
  init:     build W → cache W in model-state slot s
  execute:  get_cached(context, slot=s) → use W

Example slot allocation
  next slot s = 0
  context slot count: 0 → 1

The slot contains runtime model state when init later executes; the compiler is currently creating the operations that manage it. This example illustrates the mechanism, not a claim that the attention graph has one final slot. Its attention result depends on per-call Q/K/V values, so that computation is not an invariant result that can be precomputed during init. ↗ ExecInvariantCodeMotionPass.cpp:846 ↗ fused_attention.py:57 ↗ fused_attention.py:78

QnA 5 · Does gpu:0 automatically enable device-graph capture?

No. Device placement and device-graph mode are separate settings. Graph.__init__ defaults is_device_graph=False; it adds the graph marker only when requested. The fused-attention caller omits this option. ↗ graph.py:831 ↗ graph.py:915 ↗ fused_attention.py:41

This fused-attention example
  tensor placement      = gpu:0
  graph is_device_graph = False
  StageDeviceGraphs     → no staging for this unmarked model
  FinalizeDeviceGraphs  → returns for this unmarked model
  EmitMojo              → still emits the ordinary runtime routines

Comparison: a marked model
  stage device operations
    → partition collectives
    → build dependency/stub information
    → finalize collective graph operations

The guard is explicit in both native passes. GPU execution still occurs later through the ordinary generated routines and device context; using a GPU does not imply that this compile has constructed a captured device graph. ↗ StageDeviceGraphsPass.cpp:197 ↗ FinalizeDeviceGraphsPass.cpp:381 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:417

QnA 7 · Why are there two helper ABIs, and what does the runtime receive?

FuncOp::emitMojo distinguishes the direct MOGG ABI helper from the MGP ABI entry obtained from an asynchronous routine. The direct helper accepts pointers/dimensions/context. The runtime-facing entry takes a pointer to argument slots and handles async-value ownership and return slots. ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1326 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1334 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1420

Schematic call relationship
  runtime entry, ABI=MGP
  └─ pointer to slots
     ├─ take ownership of async input slots
     ├─ unpack handles; preserve their lifetime
     ├─ call direct helper @F_attention, ABI=MOGG
     │  └─ four tensor pointers + device context
     │     └─ build views; call FusedAttention.execute
     └─ publish returned chain/value slots

No dynamic-dimension argument is needed for static [32,32].
Any final runtime slot list also reflects later wrapper/primitive fusion.

The MGP entry is exported and non-raising; preceding passes arrange error handling. The MOGG helper can raise and is not the exported pointer-to-slots entry. This makes the low-level runtime boundary explicit without claiming that the earlier five direct arguments are the complete final runtime slot array. ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1347 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1377 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1453 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:476

QnA 8 · What replaces the helper IR, and when do machine code and MEF appear?

The emitted text becomes an MLIR resource named mojo. The pass stores its bytes in a DenseResourceElementsAttr, collects the symbols referenced by each model's mogg.compiled.call operations and inserts a mogg.compiled.load at the start of that model's init block. It then erases the emitted mogg.func operations. ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:228 ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:241 ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:255 ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:276

BEFORE EmitMojo
  IR1 module
  ├─ mgp.model @fused_attention
  │  ├─ init plan
  │  └─ execute plan → compiled.call @entry
  └─ mogg.func helpers containing code-generation operations

AFTER EmitMojo, schematic
  IR1 module
  ├─ resource "mojo" = bytes of emitted Mojo source
  └─ mgp.model @fused_attention
     ├─ init: compiled.load(symbols=[@entry], resource="mojo")
     └─ execute: compiled.call @entry(...)

The helper code is now text in the resource.
The model's runtime plan is still represented in IR.

Despite the operation name compiled.load, its resource at this point holds source text for the next compiler stage. EmitMojo can optionally dump a .mojo file, but the in-memory resource is the normal handoff. It also removes the module's device-info mapping once emission has consumed it. ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:223 ↗ EmitMojo.cpp:284

After the MGP pipeline ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:616
├─ JitCompileKernels → parse emitted Mojo with package imports ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:618 ↗ JitCompileKernels.cpp:547
│  └─ lower/compile or reuse eligible native-code cache entries ↗ JitCompileKernels.cpp:567 ↗ JitCompileKernels.cpp:575
├─ LowerCompiledRoutines → runtime load/execute operations ↗ LowerCompiledRoutines.cpp:102
└─ convertMGPToMEF → serialize the runtime program and resources ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:692

C1 completion comes after these later compilation/serialization steps.
Calling EmitMojo alone has not generated a PTX or cubin artifact.

The existing GPU artifact / ABI / driver deep dive continues from that later boundary. The caller creates Q/K/V numeric arrays and GPU buffers after compilation and model initialization; these emitted expressions are not those arrays. ↗ fused_attention.py:74 ↗ fused_attention.py:78

QnA 9 · How do MGP passes simplify shapes and chains, reuse and plan buffers, move invariant work, defer allocations, emit routine interfaces and prepare marked models for device-graph construction? Show nine worked transformations with source code, test entry points and the actual fused-attention route.

SOURCE + TEST · Each example identifies its input representation and native implementation. The before/after IR is schematic unless explicitly quoted from a test. TEST means the repository's supplied input and expected output were inspected; no compiler or GPU workload was executed. A RUN line gives an independent test pipeline, and its CHECK comments constrain printed IR or emitted source. These test files are not callees in the production compiler.

Example 1 · When does a tensor dimension become a constant, an existing SSA value, or a retained runtime query?

SOURCE · Canonicalization acts on tensor-spec metadata. The attention output spec knows both dimensions, so querying either extent can fold to 32 : index. This leaves the underlying tensor data and storage handles intact. Dimension folder

BEFORE · schematic static attention metadata
  %spec = tensor_spec.create <32x32xf32>           # No dynamic operands.
  %n = tensor_spec.get_dim[0] %spec               # Query row extent.
  %d = tensor_spec.get_dim[1] %spec               # Query column extent.
  %bytes = %n × %d × 4                            # f32 payload arithmetic.
  %buf = buffer.alloc(%guard,%bytes,%gpu,A)         # One output allocation.

AFTER · fold/canonicalize, then eligible CSE
  %c32 = index.constant 32                        # Shared extent value.
  %bytes = index.constant 4096                    # Constant payload size.
  %buf = buffer.alloc(%guard,%bytes,%gpu,A)         # Same storage role.
  %spec = tensor_spec.create <32x32xf32>           # Still describes output.

BEFORE · dynamic extent explicitly constructed
  %spec = tensor_spec.create(%batch) : <?x4xf32>   # One runtime dimension.
  %n = tensor_spec.get_dim[0] %spec               # Query what create received.
  %d = tensor_spec.get_dim[1] %spec               # Query static second axis.

AFTER
  use %batch wherever %n was used                 # Forward the same SSA value.
  use 4 : index wherever %d was used              # Static type component.

The implementation first validates the axis, then distinguishes the static type component from the defining TensorSpecCreateOp. These are the exact two successful return paths. Static and dynamic cases

if (!specType.isDynamicDim(getAxis())) {
  auto indexTy = IndexType::get(getContext());
  uint64_t dim = specType.getDims()[getAxis()].value();
  return IntegerAttr::get(indexTy, dim);
}
if (auto specCreate = dyn_cast_or_null<TensorSpecCreateOp>(specProducer)) {
  return specCreate.getRuntimeDims()[specType.getDynamicDimIndex(getAxis())];
}
Input to the query Fold result Example
spec<32x32xf32>, axis 0 Integer attribute 32 32×32×4 = 4096 bytes
create(%batch):spec<?x4xf32>, axis 0 Existing %batch operand batch=5 means 80 bytes
Function argument spec<?x4xf32>, axis 0 No fold from this rule Runtime source must supply the extent
spec<?x64x?xf32>, axis 4 Invalid IR: axis ≥ rank Diagnostic before a successful transformation

The folder returns no replacement for a dynamic argument spec whose creator is unavailable. Knowing rank two alone does not supply its batch length. Returning an SSA value also does not freeze its value across invocations. No-fold return

TEST · The diagnostic input checks the contract this fold assumes. mgp-errors.mlir feeds MGP operations directly to mo-opt --split-input-file --verify-diagnostics --allow-unregistered-dialect, without a transformation pass. Its expected-error for get_dim[4] on rank three matches TensorSpecGetDimOp::verify. The same file supplies only one dynamic operand for <?x64x?xf32> and expects a two-operands-required error from TensorSpecCreateOp::verify. These negative tests verify legal inputs; they are not evidence that the static fold was executed here. Axis diagnostic input Create diagnostic input Native verifiers Axis verifier

For attention, these metadata simplifications do not evaluate softmax(QKᵀ)V or merge the Q/K/V/O buffers merely because they share the same type. ↗ fused_attention.py:57 ↗ LoweringState.cpp:808

Example 2 · How can a chain merge disappear while every required dependency remains?

TEST · mgp-simplify-chains.mlir already contains MGP models and GRT chains. Its RUN applies the async-dataflow test analysis, --mgp-simplify-chains and --cse with unregistered stand-in operations. It checks graph structure, not their execution. Test pipeline

BEFORE · schematic subset of @chains
  %c1 = grt.chain.create(%entry)                  # Singleton dependency.
  %c2 = grt.chain.create(%c1,%c1)                  # Duplicate dependency.
  %a  = workA(%c2)                               # A waits for entry.
  %m  = grt.chain.create(%entry,%a)               # A already implies entry.
  %b  = workB(%m)                                # B needs A's completion.
  mef.output %b                                  # Publish completion of B.

AFTER
  %a  = workA(%entry)                            # Same A dependency.
  %b  = workB(%a)                                # Same B dependency.
  mef.output %b                                  # Same completion contract.

Another eligible form:
  merge(merge(%a,%b),%c) → merge(%a,%b,%c)         # Flatten a merge tree.
  merge(%a,%a) → %a                              # Remove repeated operand.

Skipped comparison:
  %a = independentA()                            # No dependency on b.
  %b = independentB()                            # No dependency on a.
  merge(%a,%b) stays a two-input dependency       # Both completions required.

The implementation flattens grt.chain.create inputs into unique primitive dependencies. It then walks each producer's gating operands and removes a candidate dependency only if another retained dependency implies it. Strict producers contribute their operands; control flow contributes only its strict extra operands; a non-strict operation contributes none. These conditions prevent a mere textual operand from being treated as a proven wait. Flattening and gating rules

if (isa<MEF::NonStrictInterface>(op))
  return ValueRange{};
return op->getOperands();

After computing the reduced sets, the pass changes each chain operation's operands, then invokes its canonicalization patterns. That second step removes singleton/empty/redundant structure exposed by the analysis. Rewriting phase

for (auto &[chainOp, values] : cache)
  chainOp.setInputChains(values);

RewritePatternSet patterns(&getContext());
GRT::ChainCreateOp::getCanonicalizationPatterns(patterns, &getContext());

The @chains checks require some.op1 to consume the entry chain and its successors to consume the first operation's chain. The consecutive-merge test expects three independent chains to remain in one merge; the uniquing test expects the original producer's chain at the output. Thus the test covers both redundant edges and dependencies that must stay. Transitive redundancy checks Independent inputs retained Duplicate elimination

Attention connection: a redundant merge(entry,entry) around a static tensor view may simplify. The async attention call still reads Q/K/V and writes O. Removing a redundant merge leaves that call and its output guard in place; it is not numerical constant folding or proof that a GPU launch has completed. ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:751 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:999

Example 3 · Why can the third temporary reuse the first, but the middle temporary cannot?

TEST · mgp-simple-buffer-reuse.mlir enters as a model with three allocations. Its RUN applies only --mgp-simple-buffer-reuse to each split input, accepting unregistered kernel_execute placeholders. The placeholders encode buffer use and chain order; they are not arithmetic kernels run by this test. Test entry and topology

BEFORE · illustrative f32[32,32] temporaries, 4096 bytes each
  %A = alloc(%entry,%size,%gpu,align=A0)           # First temporary.
  %B = alloc(%entry,%size,%gpu,align=A0)           # Second temporary.
  %C = alloc(%entry,%size,%gpu,align=A0)           # Third temporary.
  %c0 = add_one(%entry,%X,%A)                     # A = X+1.
  %c1 = times_two(%c0,%A,%B)                      # B = 2A; final read of old A.
  %c2 = minus_three(%c1,%B,%C)                    # C = B-3.
  %Y = tensor.create(%c2,%C,%spec)                # Return C's contents.

AFTER · eligible reuse
  %A = alloc(%entry,%size,%gpu,align=A0)           # Retained allocation.
  %B = alloc(%entry,%size,%gpu,align=A0)           # Still needed beside A.
  %c0 = add_one(%entry,%X,%A)                     # Write generation 1 of A.
  %c1 = times_two(%c0,%A,%B)                      # Read generation 1 of A.
  %c2 = minus_three(%c1,%B,%A)                    # Write generation 2 of A.
  %Y = tensor.create(%c2,%A,%spec)                # Rewired result buffer.

  X=[1,2,3,4] → A=[2,3,4,5] → B=[4,6,8,10] → Y=[1,3,5,7]
  allocation capacity: 12288 → 8192 bytes         # Arithmetic, not measured peak.

The reuse key compares the same SSA size value, device attribute and alignment. Earlier CSE may make duplicate size constants share an SSA definition; this pass itself does not prove arbitrary arithmetic expressions equal. Reuse key

bool operator==(const ReuseKey &other) const {
  return size == other.size && device == other.device &&
         alignment == other.alignment;
}

For A and C, every C use follows every A use through c1. A and B share the times_two operation, and B and C share minus_three, so those pairs cannot alias. The implementation rejects any shared operation first, then requires every current use to execute after every candidate use. On success it rewrites all users and erases the redundant allocation.   currentAlloc->replaceAllUsesWith(candidateAlloc);
  currentAlloc->erase();

A / B Rejected One operation reads A while writing B
Same capacity, different device or alignment Rejected Different ReuseKey
A / C with an additional late read of A Rejected unless all-use ordering is proved Old A contents remain live

TEST · mgp-exec-invariant-code-motion.mlir supplies MGP init/execute blocks. Its RUN applies --mgp-exec-invariant-code-motion --canonicalize --cse, independently of graph lowering. @liftable_op retrieves an external 37632-byte weight named foo during execute; init starts with two context slots. Input and checks

BEFORE · schematic @liftable_op
  init:
    %ctx = context.create 2                       # Slots 0,1 already reserved.
    %ready = runtime.create(%initChain,%ctx[1])   # Existing initialization.
    output %ready,%ctx,%weights,%cpu              # State passed to execute.
  execute:
    %name = string.create "foo"                   # Fixed registry key.

                                                    # Invariant retrieval.
    output %entry,%W                              # Buffer needed every call.

AFTER · eligible motion
  init:
    %ctx = context.create 3                       # One new buffer-cache slot.
    %ready = runtime.create(%initChain,%ctx[1])   # Retained initialization.
    %W = buffer.constant.external(%ready,%weights["foo",37632,align=16])

    %cached = buffer.cache(%cacheGuard,%ctx[2],%W) # Retain buffer in model state.
    output merge(%ready,%cached),%ctx,%weights,%cpu # Init waits for cache setup.
  execute:
    %W = buffer.get_cached(%entry,%ctx[2])        # Read same initialized value.
    output %entry,%W                              # Same result contract.

The analyses repeatedly exclude work that depends on per-call inputs, work trivial to recompute when only unliftable users need it, and buffers mutated by work remaining in execute. They then decide which pure producers need a clone in both blocks. This is a fixed-point dataflow decision rather than a rule that every constant-shaped allocation must move. Analysis order

For a lifted buffer still used in execute, the transformation creates a cache operation in init and a matching lookup in execute. It replaces only uses that stay in execute, then moves the original producer before init's terminator. Buffer rewrite

    executeState->builder, op->getLoc(), executeState->getContext(),
    executeState->getRootChain(), currBufferSlot,
    oldBuffer.getType());
oldBuffer.replaceUsesWithIf(newBuffer, isOpOperandUnliftable);

MGPBufferBuilder::cache takes the current slot count as the new slot index, then increments the count. That is the native reason for slot=2 and numSlots:2→3 in this test; neither is a pointer address. Slot allocation

uint64_t bufferSlot = contextCreateOp.getNumSlots();
contextCreateOp.setNumSlots(bufferSlot + 1);

  if (externalConstOp.getDHasAlias())

Example 5 · How do several GPU allocations become one pool with planned slices?

TEST · mgp-dynamic-memory-planning.mlir supplies allocation/use chains directly. Its RUN applies --mgp-dynamic-memory-planning to split MGP inputs, allowing the stand-in "use" operation. It does not run the preceding simple-reuse pass, so @basic_memory_planning intentionally still contains two same-size allocations. Test pipeline

The native planner examines top-level execute allocations on non-CPU devices. It requires known, nonempty uses that the dependency tree can order and a size computable from allowed metadata/arithmetic operations. It then groups candidates per device and requires at least two. Eligibility and grouping

if (allocOp.getDevice().getLabel() == kCPULabel)
  continue;
BEFORE · illustrative gpu:0 plan, sizes known from this call's metadata
  %A = alloc(%entry,%sizeA,%gpu,align=16)          # sizeA=16 bytes, f32[4].
  %B = alloc(%entry,%sizeB,%gpu,align=16)          # sizeB=48 bytes, f32[12].
  %cA = use_A(%entry,%A)                          # Last use of A.
  %cB = use_B(%cA,%B)                             # First use of B follows A.
  output %cB                                     # Preserve work completion.

AFTER · schematic MGP
  %high,%offA,%offB = buffer.plan(%sizeA,%sizeB)   # Compute layout when sizes known.
    alignments=[16,16], canShare=[[0,1],[1,0]]     # Disjoint-use permission.
  %pool = alloc(%entry,%high,%gpu,align=16)        # One owning allocation.
  %A,%B = buffer.bulk_slice(%pool,%gpu,
                 offsets=[%offA,%offB],sizes=[%sizeA,%sizeB])
                                                    # Two planned buffer handles.
  %cA = use_A(%entry,%A)                          # Same operation and contents.
  %cB = use_B(%cA,%B)                             # Same dependency.
  output %cB                                     # Same completion.

One permitted layout for sizeA=16,sizeB=48:
  offsets=[0,0], capacity=48 bytes                # Reuse range after A ends.
  symbolic pool base B; both slices start at B    # No observed address claimed.

The transformation computes canShare[i][j] by checking whether all uses of one allocation follow all uses of the other, in either direction. It emits BufferPlanOp, uses its high-watermark result for the pool size, and constructs one BufferBulkSliceOp. It replaces each original allocation's users with the corresponding slice result and erases the old allocation. Sharing proof Pool/slice construction

allocs[i].alloc->replaceAllUsesWith(
    ValueRange{bulkSliceOp.getOutBuffers()[i]});
allocsToDelete.push_back(allocs[i].alloc);

The numeric offsets above are an illustrative legal layout, not an inspected runtime result. If A has another use after B, sharing becomes illegal: canShare=[[0,0],[0,0]]. A separate layout such as offA=0, offB=16, capacity=64 preserves both live ranges. A tensor view of A does not end A's lifetime; consumers reached through tensor.create → tensor.extract.buffer still count. Overlapping-view test

@basic_memory_planning One buffer.plan, one allocation, one two-result bulk_slice; no individual buffer.slice
@cpu_allocations_ignored GPU pool created; CPU allocation remains
@single_allocation_not_planned CHECK-NOT: mgp.buffer.plan
@different_alignments Alignment list [16,32,64]; pool alignment 64
@tensor_view_extends_lifetime canShare = [0,0,0,0]

Defer implementation

if (!mutator)

allocOp->moveBefore(mutator->getOwner());
movedAllocOps.insert(allocOp);

Example 7 · How does an asynchronous region become a callable symbol and a pointer-to-slots runtime entry?

BEFORE · schematic isolated ReLU region
  %c1 = routine.async(%entry,%Xbuf,%Ybuf,%cpu)     # Four ordinary operands.
    ^body(ac,ax,ay,actx)                          # Four async-wrapped arguments.
      xptr = rebind(unpack(ax))                   # Input raw pointer.
      yptr = rebind(unpack(ay))                   # Output raw pointer.
      ctx  = rebind(unpack(actx))                 # Device context handle.

      ready = async.ready                        # Success result.
      output ready                               # One chain result.

AFTER · model IR
  %c1 = compiled.call @F_relu_async(%entry,%Xbuf,%Ybuf,%cpu)

AFTER · module sibling
  mogg.func @F_relu_async(ac,ax,ay,actx), ABI=MGP  # Async argument types retained.
    original region body                         # takeBody moves its block.
  mogg.func @F_relu(xptr,yptr,ctx), ABI=MOGG        # Direct helper remains separate.

Illustrative X=[-2,0,3,-1] → Y=[0,0,3,0]           # Computation preserved.

The native constructor labels the new function ABIKind::MGP, uses takeBody, registers its unique name in the symbol table, constructs CompiledCallOp and replaces the region's result users with the call's results. Body ownership transfer Call/result replacement

kernelOp->replaceAllUsesWith(callOp);
kernelOp.erase();

ABI selection Slot ownership and return offsets

Slot in this isolated four-operand example Role
0 Async input chain
1 Async reference to X buffer
2 Async reference to Y destination buffer
3 Async device-context value
4 Destination slot for returned chain

The emitter calculates result slot indices with i + numArguments. Thus the one chain result uses slot 4 in this example; Y is already supplied as a destination buffer and is not an additional by-value result. The slots carry handles/references, not an inline copy of all tensor elements. Result-slot mapping

                                                  # New build-time region.
      ^graph(%builder,%modelCtx,%xin:f32[2,3])    # Builder, context, tensor.
        %R = test.identity(%xin)                 # Original operation cloned.
        %c = test.make_chain()                   # Cloned; no longer yielded.
        device_graph.yield %R                    # Graph signature excludes chain.
    mogg.output pack(%g)                        # Publish graph handle.
  %done,%Y = device_graph.collective.execute(%G,inputs=[%X])
                                                  # Fresh completion + tensor.
  mef.output %done,%Y                            # Old users now consume execute.

Graph type: (f32[2,3] on gpu:0) → (f32[2,3] on gpu:0)
  six input elements → six identity output elements # No chain in graph I/O.

Finalization gathers non-chain captures and yields, resolves each graph device to an execute-block context, and constructs the async build wrapper. Inside that wrapper it creates the cache lookup and DeviceGraphCollectiveCreateOp. It clones each old region into the create operation, mapping the old builder and captured values to the new arguments, and omits chain values from its yields. Unlike staging's move, these clones belong to the replacement create operation; the original collective is erased after its users are rewired. Region interface Wrapper and create construction Clone and remap

The create operation's graph-body block receives a builder, a model context and the region's tensor inputs. Its graph type describes only the explicit tensor inputs and yielded outputs; the builder and context are construction parameters. Block arguments and graph signature

Value executeChain = executeOp.getChain();
unsigned outputIdx = 0;
for (Value result : collectiveOp.getResults()) {
  if (isChain(result))
    result.replaceAllUsesWith(executeChain);
  else
    result.replaceAllUsesWith(executeOp.getOutputs()[outputIdx++]);
}

This rewrite preserves the host completion contract: each old collective chain result is replaced by the new execute operation's chain, while tensor results map in order. The test checks a chain-free !mgp.device_graph signature and requires mef.output to use the execute operation's fresh chain and tensor result. Its unregistered test.identity and test.make_chain operations are structural placeholders, so the six-element identity above is illustrative arithmetic, not a numerical test result. Native result replacement Signature and result CHECKs

Condition Native outcome and inspected evidence
Marked model with eligible execute routines Staging encloses the routines; the first fixture checks its inputs, body and results
Marked model with no staged operations Staging returns without creating an empty region
Unmarked GPU model Staging leaves its routine in execute; finalization returns at the model guard
Prepared collective whose device has no execute context Finalization reports an error instead of selecting a different device

The staging test's @not_dg checks that mogg.routine.async remains and mgp.device_graph.staging does not appear. The finalization test deliberately supplies an unmarked staging input and checks that it stays unchanged without a collective create operation. The diagnostic test applies the finalization pass with --verify-diagnostics and expects the missing-device-context error, matching collectDeviceContexts. Empty staged set Unmarked staging test Unmarked finalization test Missing-context test Native context validation

Actual attention connection: the default unmarked fused_attention model follows the ordinary async routine, outlining and emission path described in Examples 7–8. The marked fixtures above explain what the compiler prepares when the marker is present.   Op<MOGGDialect, mnemonic, traits>;

  let cppNamespace = "::M::MOGG";
}

  ]>;

class MOGG_KernelTerminatorOp<string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
  MOGG_Op<mnemonic, traits # [
    DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MOGG_KernelTerminator>,
    Terminator,
  ]>;

def MOGG_ConcatOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"concat", [
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  MO_SingleDevice,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Concat Operation along axis zero";
  let description = [{
    Example:

    ```mlir
    %arg0: !mo.tensor<[3, 3], f32>
    %arg1: !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>
    %res = mogg.concat(%arg0, %arg1) : (
      !mo.tensor<[3, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>
    ) -> !mo.tensor<[5, 3], f32>
    ```

    Works for CUDA and host devices.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins Variadic<MO_Tensor>:$inputs);
  let results = (outs MO_Tensor:$result);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $inputs `)` attr-dict `:` functional-type($inputs, results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_SplitOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"split", [Pure]> {
  let summary = "Split Operation along axis zero";
  let description = [{
    `mo.split` with `axis` zero; the split sizes are implied by the result
    types.

    Example:

    ```mlir
    %input: !mo.tensor<[9, 8], f32>
    %res = mogg.split(%input) : (!mo.tensor<[9, 8], f32> ) ->
    (!mo.tensor<[2, 8], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3, 8], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4, 8], f32>)
    ```

    Currently only for the 'host' device.
    TODO: Generalize to arbitrary devices.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins MO_Tensor:$input);
  let results = (outs Variadic<MO_Tensor>:$results);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` `(`
      qualified(type($input)) `)` `->` `(` type($results) `)`
  }];
}

def MOGG_SliceOp : MOGG_Op<"slice", [
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  MO_SingleDeviceWithHostOperands<["start", "stop"]>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Contiguous zero-copy slice op lowerable to mgp.tensor.slice";
  let description = [{
    Unlike mo.slice, not lowered to a kernel by MOToMOGG. FuseViews lowers it
    to a mogg.routine temporarily and raises it back if unfused.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MO_Tensor:$input,
    MO_IndexScalarIfRanked:$start,
    MO_IndexScalarIfRanked:$stop
  );
  let results = (outs MO_Tensor:$result);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_CallOp : MOGG_Op<"call", [
  MOGG_CallLike,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
  MOGG_FuncCallOpInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Calls into an outlined stub";

  let arguments = (ins
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$name,
    Variadic<AnyType>:$inputs,
    OptionalAttr<I64Attr>:$affinity_device_id
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$outputs);

    $name ($inputs^ `:` type($inputs))? (`->` type($outputs)^)?

  }];
}

def MOGG_CallAsyncOp : MOGG_Op<"call.async", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
  MOGG_FuncCallOpInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Calls into an outlined stub asynchronously";
  let description = [{
    Dispatches via Mojo `create_task`. `affinity_device_id` pins the task to a
    CPU core with NUMA affinity for that GPU. It is a plain integer because
    kernel-layer device refs are label-only.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$name,
    Variadic<AnyType>:$inputs,
    OptionalAttr<I64Attr>:$affinity_device_id
  );
  let results = (outs MOGG_TaskHandle:$task_handle);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $name (`(` $inputs^ `:` type($inputs) `)`)?
    (`affinity_device_id` `=` $affinity_device_id^)? attr-dict
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    FuncOp getCallee();
  }];
}

def MOGG_CallBuildGraphOp : MOGG_Op<"call.build_graph", [
  AttrSizedOperandSegments,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MOGG_KernelCallInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Record a kernel's `build_graph` function into a device-graph builder";
  let description = [{
    The device-graph counterpart of `mogg.call.execute`: invokes `build_graph`
    against a builder instead of `execute` against a context, recording a node
    rather than running the kernel. Produces no result; the enclosing
    `mgp.device_graph.dependencies` op orders nodes. Not a kernel terminator,
    and not wrapped in `mogg.with_trace`.

    `$hasEpilogueFusion` mirrors `mogg.call.opaque`: it is copied from the
    dispatch this call records and set the kernel's `has_epilogue_fusion`
    parameter, so a fused body reaches `build_graph` the same way it reaches
    `execute`.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    mogg.call.build_graph["linalg_kernels.__init__.Matmul"]
        inputs(%in, %wt : !mo.tensor<...>, !mo.tensor<...>)
        outputs(%out : !mo.tensor<...>)
        builder(%builder)

    // Lowered to
    Matmul.build_graph[...](out, in, wt, builder)
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    StrAttr:$kernelSymName,
    StrAttr:$moOpName,
    UnitAttr:$isThrows,
    Variadic<AnyTypeOf<[MOGG_Tensor, MOGG_Buffer, MOGG_Scalar, MOGG_Tuple,
                        MO_Opaque]>>:$inputs,
    Variadic<AnyTypeOf<[MOGG_Tensor, MOGG_Buffer, MOGG_Scalar, MOGG_Tuple,
                        MO_Opaque]>>:$outputs,
    MGP_DeviceGraphBuilderType:$graphBuilder,
    OptionalAttr<DictionaryAttr>:$kernel_param,
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$hasEpilogueFusion
  );

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `[` $kernelSymName `]` `` custom<OptionalKernelParams>($kernel_param)
    (`inputs` `(` $inputs^ `:` qualified(type($inputs)) `)`)?
    (`outputs` `(` $outputs^ `:` qualified(type($outputs)) `)`)?
    `builder` `(` $graphBuilder `)`
    (`isThrows` $isThrows^)?
    `moOpName` `=` $moOpName
    (`hasEpilogueFusion` `=` $hasEpilogueFusion^)?
    attr-dict
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;
}


def MOGG_AsyncRoutineOp : MOGG_Op<"routine.async", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
  DeclInterface,
  IsolatedFromAbove,
  MO_ExplicitDevice,
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  SingleBlockImplicitTerminator<"MOGG::OutputOp">,
]> {
  let summary = "An abstract function representing a compiled body of code";
  let description = [{
    Takes and returns AsyncValues and runs its body to completion (always
    blocking). A generic form of mogg.routine; the first result is a mef.chain.

    Sequence fusion (concatenating code) fuses a parent region into a child:
    `canFuseIntoOther` allows this region as parent, `canBeFusedInto` as
    child. `canDuplicate` lets a region with several children be copied into
    each of them.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    Variadic<AnyType>:$operands,
    MO_ParamDecls:$outputParamDecls,
    M_InOutSignatureAttr:$inOutSignature,
    OptionalAttr<MOGG_FusionInfoAttr>:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    DefaultValuedAttr<ArrayAttr, "{}">:$constantResources,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canFuseIntoOther,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canBeFusedInto,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canDuplicate,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$isStructured
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$results);
  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$body);
  let hasCanonicalizeMethod = 1;
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    custom<ImmediateDispatch>($dispatch)
    custom<Kernel>($operands, type($operands), type($results), $body,
                   $outputParamDecls)
    custom<FusionInfo>($fusionInfo)
    (`canBeFusedInto` `=` $canBeFusedInto^)?
    (`canDuplicate` `=` $canDuplicate^)?
    (`canFuseIntoOther` `=` $canFuseIntoOther^)?
    (`constantResources` `=` $constantResources^)?
    `inOutSignature` `=` $inOutSignature
    (`isStructured` `=` $isStructured^)?
    attr-dict
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Required by DeclInterface.
    ArrayRef<ParamDeclAttr> getInputParams() { return {}; }

    Block &getBodyBlock() { return getBody().front(); }

    MOGG::OutputOp getBodyTerminator();
  }];
}

def MOGG_CompiledLoadOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"compiled.load"> {
  let summary = "Loads pairs of (symbol, compiled object) into the runtime "
                "for a given device.";
  let description = [{
    Registers each symbol with its compiled-object blob in the runtime, for
    use by ops like `CompiledCallOp`. The object format and registration
    depend on the op's device.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ArrayAttr:$symbols,
    ConfinedAttr<
      ElementsAttr,
      [AnyAttrOf<[Builtin_DenseResourceElementsAttr]>]
    >:$value,
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$debuginfo
  );
}


def MOGG_CompiledCallOp : MOGG_Op<"compiled.call", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MemoryEffectsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MO_ParamDeclaration>,
  MO_ExplicitDevice,
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Executes a compiled kernel on a given device.";
  let description = [{
    Looks up the compiled object (loaded by `CompiledLoadOp`) by name
    and calls it with the lowered operands.

    `usedParams` are the shape parameters the kernel uses; they are passed at
    runtime to reconstruct tensor shapes. `outputParamDecls` defines parameter
    values, which MGP translates into parameter system calls. `dispatch` says
    how the runtime schedules the call (see `MOGG_DispatchKind`).

    The kernel reads and writes memory its operands only point to, such as
    the buffer an init-block call fills, so the op is never pure: a call
    whose results are unused is not dead, and two identical calls are not
    redundant.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    Variadic<AnyType>:$operands,
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$calleeSymbol,
    ArrayAttr:$usedParams,
    MO_ParamDecls:$outputParamDecls,
    OptionalAttr<MOGG_FusionInfoAttr>:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    ArrayAttr:$constantResources
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$results);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $calleeSymbol `` custom<OutputParamDecls>($outputParamDecls)
    `` `(` $operands `)`
    custom<ImmediateDispatch>($dispatch)
    custom<FusionInfo>($fusionInfo)
    `constantResources` `=` $constantResources `,`
    `usedParams` `=` $usedParams
    attr-dict `:` functional-type($operands, $results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_FuncOp : MOGG_Op<"func", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  FunctionOpInterface,
  IsolatedFromAbove,
  SingleBlockImplicitTerminator<"MOGG::OutputOp">,
  SymbolName,
  SymbolVisibility,
  Symbol,
]> {
  let summary = "Op that outlines a kernel";
  let description = [{
    A kernel that will be compiled to Mojo text.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins
    SymbolNameAttr:$sym_name,
    TypeAttrOf<FunctionType>:$function_type,
    MOGG_FusionInfoAttr:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    DefaultValuedAttr<ArrayAttr, "{}">:$constantResources,
    MOGG_ABIKindAttr:$abi,
    // Execution-device label for each kernel's `target` parameter. A string
    // rather than `#M.device_ref` because only the label matters.
    StrAttr:$device,
    OptionalAttr<ArrayAttr>:$trait_stub_buffer_capture,
    OptionalAttr<ArrayAttr>:$trait_stub_arg_bounds,
    // Needed by -symbol-dce.
    DefaultValuedAttr<StrAttr, "\"private\"">:$sym_visibility
  );

  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$body);

  let hasCustomAssemblyFormat = 1;
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    Block &getBodyBlock() { return getBody().front(); }
    OutputOp getBodyTerminator();
    Region *getCallableRegion() { return &getBodyRegion(); }
    ArrayRef<Type> getArgumentTypes() {
      return getFunctionType().getInputs();
    }
    ArrayRef<Type> getResultTypes() {
      return getFunctionType().getResults();
    }

    mlir::ArrayAttr getArgAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    mlir::ArrayAttr getResAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    void setArgAttrsAttr(mlir::ArrayAttr attrs){}
    void setResAttrsAttr(mlir::ArrayAttr attrs){}
    mlir::Attribute removeArgAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    mlir::Attribute removeResAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }

  private:
    mlir::LogicalResult emitMojoMGPABI(EmitMojoState &state);
    mlir::LogicalResult emitMojoMOGGABI(EmitMojoState &state);
  }];
}

def MOGG_TensorInitOp : MOGG_Op<"tensor.__init__", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  Pure,
]> {

    Lowers to a ManagedTensorSlice constructor call from a data pointer and
    dimensions.

    Variadic<SI64Scalar>:$dims,
    BoolAttr:$mut,
    MO_IOKind:$io
  );

    `(` $buffer (`,` $dims^)? `)` `io` `=` custom<IOKind>($io) `,` `mut` `=` $mut
    attr-dict `:` qualified(type($buffer)) `->` qualified(type($tensor))
  }];
}

def MOGG_TensorArgInitOp : MOGG_Op<"tensor_arg.__init__", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  AttrSizedOperandSegments,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Construct a trait-lane tensor argument from its contract";
  let description = [{
    Like `mogg.tensor.__init__`, but carries the `#mogg.tensor_arg` contract
    for an argument satisfying a kernel trait bound, instead of `{io, mut}`.
    `role`/`access` are read from the contract, not the result type.

    `$device_context` is for the GPU emit path and is not yet populated.
    `contract.fused` is currently always false and `contract.access` `none`.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    Variadic<SI64Scalar>:$dims,
    Optional<MOGG_Context>:$device_context,
    MOGG_TensorArgContractAttr:$contract
  );
  let results = (outs AnyTypeOf<[MO_Tensor, MO_Buffer]>:$tensor);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $buffer (`,` $dims^)? `)` (`context` `(` $device_context^ `)`)?
    `contract` `=` $contract
    attr-dict `:` qualified(type($buffer)) `->` qualified(type($tensor))
  }];
}

def MOGG_AsyncUnpackOp : MOGG_Op<"async.unpack", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
  Pure,
  TypesMatchWith<"input is the async wrapper of the result",
                 /*lhs=*/"output", /*rhs=*/"input",
                 "::M::MOGG::AsyncType::get($_self)">,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_Async:$input);
  let results = (outs AnyType:$output);
  let summary = "Unpacks an async value and returns it as sync";
  let description = [{
    Projects `!mogg.async<T>` (values outside a `mogg.routine.async`)
    to `T`. Inverse of `mogg.async.pack`. Only `T` is printed.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` type($output)
  }];

  let hasFolder = 1;
}

def MOGG_AsyncPackOp : MOGG_Op<"async.pack", [

                 "::M::MOGG::AsyncType::get($_self)">,
]> {

  let results = (outs MOGG_Async:$output);
  let summary = "Packs an sync value and returns it as async";
  let description = [{
    Inverse of `mogg.async.unpack`. Only `T` is printed.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` type($input)
  }];

  let hasFolder = 1;
}

]> {

    Backs empty tensors passed to some kernels after fusion.

def MOGG_YieldOp : MOGG_Op<"yield", [

  let description = [{
    Yields the results of a mogg.try / except, the value a
    `mogg.tensor.create.prologue` body returns to the reading kernel, the
    value a compute `mogg.tensor.create.epilogue` body returns for the kernel
    to store, or an element's contribution to a `mogg.rowwise.reduce`.

  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Wraps a kernel terminator in a Trace context manager";

    Models `with Trace[...]` around the KernelTerminator of a MOGG ABI stub.
    Always throwing because Trace.__enter__ raises.
  }];

def MOGG_ProfileScopeBeginOp : MOGG_Op<"profile_scope.begin", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Opens a trace range for a Graph.profile_scope() span";
  let description = [{
    Lowers to `var t = Trace[...](name, color=...); t.start()`.

    A region-less sibling of `mogg.with_trace`: values defined inside a region
    would be invisible to later ops, and sequence-fused bodies have SSA values
    live across scope boundaries.

    `color` is set only when every covered op agrees on one (see
    `resolveProfileScopeColor`). Always throwing because `Trace.start()`
    raises.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins StrAttr:$name, OptionalAttr<StrAttr>:$color);
  let results = (outs MOGG_ProfileScopeRange:$range);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $name (`color` `=` $color^)? attr-dict
  }];
}

  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Closes the trace range opened by a `mogg.profile_scope.begin`";
  let description = [{
    Lowers to `t.end()`. Always throwing because `Trace.end()` raises.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_ProfileScopeRange:$range);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $range attr-dict
  }];
}

  }];

  let assemblyFormat = "$error attr-dict";

def MOGG_TryOp : MOGG_Op<"try", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<OpAsmOpInterface, ["getAsmBlockArgumentNames"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Op that represent a try / except statement";
  let description = [{
    The except region takes the raised `!mogg.error` as its only argument,
    printed as `except(%err)`.
  }];
  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$tryRegion, SizedRegion<1>:$exceptRegion);
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$outputs);

    $tryRegion custom<ExceptRegion>($exceptRegion)
    attr-dict `:` type($outputs)

}

def MOGG_AsyncErrorOp : MOGG_Op<"async.error", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_Error:$error);
  let results = (outs AnyType:$output);

  let summary = "Represents setting an error on a kernel output";
  let description = [{
    Sets an error on a chain or non-tensor output in a raising kernel's except
    block.

    ```
    mogg.try {
     ...
    } except(%err) {
      %chain = mogg.async.error %err : !mef.chain
      %dim0 = mogg.async.error %err : !si64
      mogg.yield %chain, %dim0
    }
    ```

    Lowers to `mogg_async_error_value`, returning an error `AnyAsyncValueRef`.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $error attr-dict `:` type(results)
  }];
}
